Both Netlify and Vercel can deploy your Hugo site directly from a Git repository. Create the …

Both Netlify and Vercel can deploy your Hugo site directly from a Git repository. Create the corresponding configuration file at the root of your project. This file defines how the site is built and which Hugo version will be used.
Security and caching#The configurations also include several optional HTTP headers that help improve the security and caching of your documentation site:
Referrer-Policy controls the referrer information sent with requests. Content-Security-Policy helps protect against cross-site scripting attacks. X-Content-Type-Options prevents browsers from incorrectly interpreting content types. X-Frame-Options prevents the site from being loaded inside a frame on another site. Strict-Transport-Security forces browsers to use HTTPS. Permissions-Policy disables browser features that the site does not need. Cache-Control allows static resources to be cached for one year. Configuration example#The following is an example configuration for Netlify and Vercel. While these files are not required, they can be useful for quickly configuring your project:
netlify.tomlvercel.jsonHugo version#Both examples use Hugo 0.164.0 because it is the minimum version required for the theme to work correctly. If you want to use a different version, make sure to update the HUGO_VERSION value in your configuration files.
